data.narrative:
EX-Fusion is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Kazuki Matsuo, Shinsuke Fujioka, and Yoshitaka Mori that has raised $37M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 total peers—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private entities spanning the same sector and stage range. The private peer set includes Fuse Energy, Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, and X-Energy, providing direct comparability to early-stage nuclear technology ventures.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using the $37M total raised as a proxy for current value, applies a standard 2.0x Series A-to-next-stage multiplier, implying a $74M valuation. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector and adjacent-stage comparables—Valar Atomics at $6.0B (Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M (Seed), and Fuse Energy at $200M (Series A)—yields a median of $808M, with a range from $200M to $6.0B.

Triangulation of these two methods produces a low estimate of $63M, a median of $441M, and a high estimate of $929M. The wide spread reflects substantial variance within the nuclear energy peer set, particularly the 30x gap between the lowest and highest comparable valuations. Key uncertainties include the precise stage and operational progress of each peer relative to EX-Fusion, and whether early-stage private nuclear ventures command premiums or discounts to publicly traded comparables. A valuation range of $200M–$600M appears most defensible given peer overlap at the Series A level.
